result.title: Identity protocol review
result.text: Security proposal: OIDC authorization code flow with PKCE for the first integration, exact redirect URI validation, issuer/audience/signature/expiry checks, replay protection, and safe account linking. This does not settle the commercial SAML requirement in SSO-14. Evaluate managed federation support against direct implementation. Primary sources: https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html ; https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9700.html ; https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63c/Federation/ . NIST guidance is a reference, not proof a private product has a legal obligation. See workspace://docs/privacy and workspace://docs/accessibility.

result.title: #identity session correction
result.text: Leo, engineering: Correction to my earlier note: removing a member does NOT revoke existing sessions today. They expire after 24 hours. Security wants this explicit in the PRD and acceptance tests. Mina: Contract admins still need an answer on guest accounts and SAML versus OIDC scope.

result.title: Current authentication architecture
result.text: Architecture authority: current deployed system. Password and magic link only. Global users are identified by internal UUID; memberships are tenant scoped with separate roles. Email can change and is not a stable federated identity key. Web server owns sessions; mobile clients exchange short-lived handoff codes. The spring SAML prototype was abandoned, never shipped. Decision trail: workspace://docs/identity-review. Operational detail: workspace://docs/sessions. Schema: workspace://docs/identity-schema.

result.title: Enterprise single sign-on request
result.text: Prospect Cedar Labs requires SAML 2.0 with Okta for its pilot. Another prospect supports OIDC with Entra ID. Need tenant configuration, a test connection and safe enforcement. No contract signed and no launch date committed. Linked review: workspace://docs/auth-architecture. Commercial addendum: workspace://contracts/cedar. Search #identity for implementation discussion.

result.title: Sessions and operations
result.text: Today disabling a workspace member prevents new login but existing sessions remain valid for up to 24 hours. SSO needs explicit deprovisioning/session-revocation policy, IdP outage handling and observable failure reasons. Security requires tested break-glass admin access with audited use, not a universal bypass. No support owner or on-call escalation SLO assigned yet. SCIM provisioning is a separate scope decision. See workspace://slack/identity/340.

result.title: Identity storage constraints
result.text: Proposed federated identity uniqueness is tenant_id plus issuer plus subject, mapped to a stable user UUID. Current membership role remains independently authorized. Tenant configuration versions must support rollback and signing-key rotation. This is a proposal needing migration review, not implemented schema. Links: workspace://docs/auth-architecture.

result.title: Identity privacy questions
result.text: Collect only required identity claims; document storage, retention and access. Neither prospect data region nor controller/processor contract terms are settled. Legal review is triggered by the inaccessible Cedar addendum and possible cross-border handling, not by assuming a jurisdiction from the company name. Contact human commercial owner for the actual contract and jurisdiction. See workspace://contracts/cedar.

result.title: Login UX accessibility requirement
result.text: Internal target is WCAG 2.2 AA for the login path. Include keyboard navigation, focus and error recovery, accessible tenant discovery, password-manager/paste compatibility for fallback, and avoid unsupported cognitive tests. Check both product UI and IdP handoff. Primary source: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/accessible-authentication-minimum.html . Treat this as a product target; no certified conformance claim exists.
